condition: subacute dull right flank misery with cloudy foul smelling urine and mild post meal nausea
level_rationale: Three days of cloudy foul-smelling urine and a dull right flank ache in a 36-year-old adult with only mild nausea after breakfast today points to a subacute urinary tract infection needing an outpatient clinic urinalysis, culture, and oral antibiotics rather than over-the-counter self-care, whereas vomiting every sip of water for 10 hours alongside 3 days of cloudy foul-smelling urine and right flank pain prevents oral hydration and oral antibiotic therapy, requiring immediate Emergency Department intravenous fluids and parenteral antibiotics.

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic facts (age 36, 3 days of cloudy foul-smelling urine, 3 days of dull right-flank pain, and mild nausea after breakfast today) with an exact 5-word vs 5-word continuous span swap and zero stated negatives. Escalating only fact f4 along the same gastrointestinal dimension from 'mild nausea after breakfast today' to 'vomiting every sip of water for 10 hours' keeps the exact urinary-flank presentation intact while crossing the unambiguous hospital admission threshold (complete inability to retain oral fluids or oral antibiotics, level 4) with unique wording under Rules A and D.
